text:
marco: kicking off handoff for the new eu-central GPU cluster bring-up. final validation done, handing to on-call SREs. TL;DR: paging thresholds, ownership, and quick runbook link below.

liz: thanks marco. can you confirm the pager thresholds and who owns infra vs runtime?

marco: infra owns provisioning/networking/quota failures. runtime owns model-serving GPUs, KV cache errors, and autoscale logic. paging thresholds we set:
- GPU memory hot: 90% sustained for 5m -> page on-call SRE (pagerduty infra-sre)
- GPU compute saturation: 95% for 2m -> page runtime-oncall -> if no ack in 10m escalate to eng-runtime lead
- Pod crashloop/backoff 3+ pods in 10m -> page on-call -> create incident stub
- Network flaps (node notReady > 3m) -> page infra oncall -> ops manager if >30m

kevin: where's the runbook? I want the exact commands to check GPU counts and PMem.

marco: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-central-gpu-bringup (bookmark it). Quick checks:
```
# check node GPU allocation
kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia_com_gpu
# check pod GPU usage (nvidia-smi via daemonset)
kubectl exec -it ds-nvtop -n infra -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
# check pod restarts
kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount>0 | grep model-server
```

alex: paging config lives in PagerDuty service: "EU-CENTRAL-GPU". I updated escalation policy: primary on-call -> oncall lead (liz) after 15m -> eng-runtime lead after 30m -> ops director for Sev2+.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New cluster eu-central-1 created by infra-ops at 1719850200. 12x A100-80GB provisioned, 4 infra nodes, 8 worker pools.

liz: training/ownership notes: on-call SRE should run the full validation checklist on first page of runbook within first hour of handoff. If any quota/networking issues appear, call infra-ops pager immediately. We also expect the first 24h to show autoscaler warm-up spikes; only page if thresholds hit.

marco: cost guardrails: autoscale max set to 12 GPUs, burst pool limited to 2 extra gpus. Billing alerts: daily cost > $5k/day -> notify finance@ and ops-manager.

kevin: escalation matrix on runbook looks good. For training: recommend new on-call shadow session (30m) with infra-ops and runtime team; schedule: send calendar invite to @oncall-sre rotation.

liz: added shadow session slot tomorrow 09:30 CET and a short lab cluster access for new on-call. Also uploaded a checklist artifact to runbook page (Validation Checklist v1.2).

marco: final handoff: infra-ops still owns rollback/provisioning. on-call SRE owns monitoring, alert triage, immediate mitigations (evacuate node, cordon, restart pods). For persistent capacity issues escalate to eng-runtime and infra-ops.

sre-oncall: acked. I'll run checks now and report back. If anything else pops up, I'll page according to policy. :thumbsup:

marco: thanks — leaving this thread open for the first 24h. add any anomalies here so we have a single audit trail.
